question: A 53-year-old male presents to your office for abdominal discomfort. The patient states he first noticed pain on his right flank several months ago, and it has been gradually getting worse. For the past week, he has also noticed blood in his urine. Prior to this episode, he has been healthy and does not take any medications. The patient denies fever, chills, and dysuria. He has a 40 pack-year smoking history. Vital signs are T 37 C, HR 140/90 mmHg, HR 84/min, RR 14/min, O2 98%. Physical exam is unremarkable. CBC reveals a hemoglobin of 17 and hematocrit of 51%, and urinalysis is positive for red blood cells, negative for leukocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking history -> Increased risk for renal cell carcinoma -> 70% CHAIN: Abdominal discomfort, right flank pain, blood in urine -> Symptoms of renal cell carcinoma -> 80% CHAIN: Hemoglobin of 17, hematocrit of 51% -> Elevated levels can be seen in renal cell carcinoma -> 75% CHAIN: Positive for red blood cells in urinalysis, negative for leukocytes -> Suggestive of renal cell carcinoma -> 85% CHAIN: Overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings -> Most likely diagnosis: Renal cell carcinoma -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of abdominal discomfort, right flank pain, blood in urine, elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit, and positive red blood cells in urinalysis are highly suggestive of renal cell carcinoma. The smoking history further increases the suspicion. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is renal cell carcinoma.
analysis: The patient's presentation of abdominal discomfort, right flank pain, blood in urine, elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit, positive red blood cells in urinalysis, and a significant smoking history strongly suggest renal cell carcinoma. The absence of leukocytes in the urinalysis makes pyelonephritis less likely. Polycystic kidney disease typically presents with different symptoms and findings. Abdominal aortic aneurysm usually does not present with hematuria. Renal oncocytoma is less common and less likely to cause the combination of symptoms seen in this patient.
